title: Vijay Drops Trichy East, Plants His Flag in Perambur
excerpt: Tamil Nadu's new CM vacates one of two won seats, triggering a by-poll and anchoring himself in Chennai's working-class north.
body:
Hours after being sworn in as Tamil Nadu's 13th Chief Minister on May 10, C. Joseph Vijay formally resigned from the Tiruchirappalli East Assembly constituency — choosing to anchor his legislative presence in Perambur, the northern Chennai seat he also won in the April 23 elections.

**What happened:**
A couple of hours after being sworn in, TVK founder Vijay resigned his MLA post from Trichy East; his resignation letter was handed to Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Secretary K. Srinivasan by Ministers K.A. Sengottaiyan and P. Venkataramanan at the State Secretariat. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate who wins two seats simultaneously must vacate one. Vijay had polled 91,381 votes in Tiruchirappalli East and a commanding 1,20,365 votes in Perambur, where he defeated DMK's R.D. Shekar by over 53,000 votes.

**Why Perambur matters:**
Vijay has chosen to continue as MLA from Perambur, and political observers note that retaining the seat gives him a stable urban base in Chennai, where administrative decisions and party coordination are more accessible. Perambur is an industrial belt with a mixed working-class population — a constituency where TVK has already penetrated the voter base, giving the party room to work at the grassroots level. The decision mirrors a precedent set by former Chief Minister J. Jayalalithaa, who resigned one of her seats after a dual victory before assuming office.

**What to watch:**
The resignation from Tiruchirappalli East will now trigger a by-election in the constituency. Meanwhile, Governor Rajendra Arlekar has directed Vijay to seek a vote of confidence in the Assembly by May 13 — the first major test of his minority government's survival.
nri_angle: For Tamil-Americans with roots in Chennai or Trichy, this seat decision signals where Vijay intends to build his political base and which communities he will prioritise as he governs India's sixth-largest state.
